Name: Belshazzar
Summary: Belshazzar was king of Babylon who, at a great feast for a thousand lords, drank wine from the gold and silver vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple, praising gods of gold and silver; a hand wrote Mene, Mene, Tekel, Upharsin on the wall, Daniel interpreted it — God had numbered his kingdom and finished it — and that very night Belshazzar was slain and Darius the Mede took the kingdom.
KeyStory: At Belshazzar's feast the fingers of a man's hand wrote on the plaster of the wall, and Daniel read the writing: thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting.
RelatedPeople: King Nebuchadnezzar; Daniel; Darius the Mede
LifeLesson: Drinking from vessels taken from God's house while praising idols is the last feast before the writing on the wall.
